data.title: Thanksgiving storm knocks out power, disrupts flights on US East Coast
data.description:
A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast on Thursday, knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of users as wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 kph) toppled trees and power lines.

Heavy rains flooded coastal areas, while utilities warned that rain-soaked ground and strong winds could increase the risk of falling trees and power outages.

Nearly 200,000 homes and businesses had no power in Virginia and another 177,000 in Maryland as of 2:26 p.m. ET (1926 GMT), according to poweroutage.us, which also showed Pennsylvania, New Jersey and North Carolina each had tens of thousands of utility customers without electricity.

Utilities and state officials had warned the combination of strong onshore winds and rain could cause widespread power disruptions.

Wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were reported or forecast across parts of Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and coastal New England, according to the US National Weather Service.

New York City Emergency Management reported winds intensified on Thursday afternoon, reaching 56 mph (90 kph) at LaGuardia Airport.

The NWS said strong onshore winds associated with the storm, combined with king tides, were causing coastal flooding in low-lying communities along portions of the East Coast.

The threat of storms had already led officials to postpone Thursday's 100th edition of the annual Macy's ​Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City, marking the first time the event has been rescheduled due to severe weather.

The storm also disrupted holiday air travel, with more than 400 US flights canceled and some 1,600 delayed by early on Thursday afternoon, according to FlightAware. Major airports in the Washington and New York City areas were among the hardest hit.

"A powerful coastal storm will continue to bring severe impacts to the region through today into this evening due to damaging high winds accompanied by heavy rainfall," the NWS said. "The storm departs overnight into Friday."

data.title: Pensions Trusted by Millions of Industrial Workers Make a Surprising Comeback — WSJ
data.description:
By Heather Gillers and Juliet Chung

Five years ago, millions of truckers, miners and other American industrial workers were in such grave danger of having their pensions cut that Congress injected cash. The real rescue came from the U.S. stock market.

Years of double-digit market gains have spurred a remarkable turnaround for multiemployer retirement plans, those pensions governed by collective bargaining agreements between a group of employers and a union. These funds fell into a dangerous limbo after suffering severe losses in the 2008-09 financial crisis, and amid the decadeslong decline of industries like mining and manufacturing.

Now, the nation's 1,176 active multiemployer plans have a combined $900 billion on hand, according to an analysis by pension consultant Milliman. That is their healthiest funding level since 2007 and, for most, it is enough money to cover the expected cost of workers' promised pension benefits. There is even a small surplus that could cushion the blow if the recent selloff continues.

"Stocks have helped a lot," said Michael Scott, executive director of the National Coordinating Committee for Multiemployer Plans, a group of employers, pension funds, unions and workers.

Other factors helped, too. Workers and employers put billions more than required into the pension funds. The shakiest plans got tens of billions of dollars from Congress. Some plans also reduced future pension benefits promised to workers. But for most of the plans, investment returns were the biggest driver of their improved health. Stocks typically made up the biggest share of those investments, according to Milliman.

Consider the Ironworkers District Council of New England pension fund, a retirement plan founded in 1957 whose nearly 5,000 workers and retirees have helped erect many of the structures that make up Boston's skyline. Ten years ago, the plan had only about 70% of the money it needed to cover pension benefits, according to the fund's investment consultant Meketa.

U.S. stocks account for the biggest share of the fund's portfolio and one of its strongest-performing asset classes. And in the past decade, they have been instrumental in restoring the full amount required to cover all future pension benefits. The plan had $770 million on hand as of Sept. 30.

It isn't all thanks to artificial intelligence or data centers either. The ironworkers' plan has been underweight the Magnificent Seven tech stocks that have led the market in recent years. The plan has a value bent, investing in passive index funds that focus on high-quality companies that cost relatively less to buy.

"They're outside every day earning every dollar that they're making," pension trustee Mike Hess said of the ironworkers whose retirement benefits are covered by the plan. "At the end of the day when they want to go and retire after putting in a hard 25 to 30 years, they expect their money to be there."

Hess, 48, followed an uncle into iron work and contributed a portion of his pay to the fund for more than two decades while installing rebar, doing ornamental work and building structures and exteriors, including for Boston's Millennium Tower.

The stakes are high. Unlike city, state and public school employees, whose pensions enjoy strong court protections and are routinely topped up with taxpayer dollars, multiemployer pensions can run out of money. The federal Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation provides backup benefits in that scenario, but someone with 30 years of work would max out at $12,870 a year.

Multiemployer pension plans cover professions ranging from musicians to bricklayers, steelworkers, roofers, woodworkers, miners and a range of other laborers. They were once stable, in large part because they were serving thriving industries. But changes across many of those industries weakened the plans.

Many also made some of the same overly optimistic investment projections and outdated lifespan calculations that have hamstrung public and corporate pensions. Then in 2008 stock losses slashed pension savings. The recession that followed put many of those laborers out of work and their pension contributions dried up.

Some pensions were still in such dire straits a decade later that Congress in 2021 approved an $80 billion bailout that has dramatically improved funding levels for 155 plans. Three dozen other plans still face deep shortfalls, with an aggregate funding level of 60%, according to the Milliman analysis. Those plans may not have been eligible for aid during the designated time period or they may have been approved for funding but were still waiting to receive it at the time of the study, said one of the authors, Nina Lantz.

The Dorchester, Mass.-based ironworkers' pension lost 26% in 2008, a devastating blow. With the economy in a recession, construction work dried up, too, meaning the pension was paying out more than it took in for several years. Typically, a portion of the pay each union member gets for an hour's work goes to the pension.

But unlike 401(k)-style "defined contribution" plans, pension funds pay out predetermined benefits even when the market underperforms. Short on cash, the ironworkers fund had to unload stocks and other investments at lows.

"We were selling out of our index funds just so we can pay the members," recalled Hess' fellow trustee, Russell Anderson, who recently retired as owner of Rockland, Mass.-based Union Steel Erectors.

Hess, who got involved with the pension in 2016 as the equivalent of a board observer and became a trustee in 2020, got into the habit of watching Bloomberg Television in his office in the union hall. He said he learned over time not to focus too much on the market's daily gyrations, knowing the plan was investing for the long haul.

Another part of the equation: getting workers' trust. For stock market gains to have a real impact, the pension fund needed more money to invest. Union members repeatedly agreed to requests from Hess and other trustees to increase the portion of their paychecks going into pension coffers.

"You try to educate the member as to why that money's needed," Hess said. "If you don't tell them why (the fund) needs to get the dollar, you're not getting that dollar."

It took the pension more than a decade to make it back to the 85% funding level it had at the beginning of 2008. It finally happened at the end of 2021 after three years of double-digit gains in the S&P 500. The following year, the pension fund increased its allocation to public equities — which meant buying more stocks in 2022, a year when the equity market tanked. The pension invests in U.S., global and emerging stock markets.

"Looking back, it seems easier than it was," said Meketa's Dan Dynan, who advises the ironworkers' pension, among other clients.

Dynan recalled moments like 2022 and the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic as difficult times for worried investors to remain committed to their stock allocations.

The ironworkers' commitment to a robust stock portfolio paid off when another three years of double-digit gains in the S&P 500 followed in 2023, 2024 and 2025, plugging a $50 million dollar shortfall and pushing the funding level above 100% this year. Recently, the plan has made moves to protect its stock gains by shifting more money into bonds and infrastructure.

"It was nice to finally see a triple-digit number," Anderson said.

Write to Heather Gillers at heather.gillers@wsj.com and Juliet Chung at Juliet.Chung@wsj.com

data.title: Ironman Announces Amendments to Working Capital Adjustment and Shareholder Loan
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

LANGLEY, BC, November 26, 2026 - TheNewswire – Ironman International Ltd. (TSXV: IMI) (OTCQB: IMITF) ("Ironman" or the "Company") announces amendments to the payment terms of four working capital adjustment promissory notes (the “Notes”) evidencing the working capital adjustment payment in the aggregate principal amount of $9,826,786 (the “Working Capital Adjustment Payment”) issued pursuant to the share exchange agreement dated December 7, 2024, as amended, pursuant to which the Company acquired 1097195 B.C. Ltd. (“109”) and Ironman Directional Drilling US Inc. (the “Transaction”), as previously described in the Company’s news release dated September 29, 2025.

Pursuant to the terms of the Notes, the Working Capital Adjustment Payment was payable in equal installments commencing 12 months from the closing date of the Transaction and continuing every 12 months thereafter over a period of 60 months. The Company has agreed with the holders of the Notes, being Michael Irmen, Denise Irmen, Robert Scott and 599837 B.C. Ltd. (“599”), to amend the Notes to defer the payment dates for the first three installments under each Note to the date that is 48 months from the closing date of the Transaction, resulting in the first four installments being due on September 26, 2029. All other terms of the Notes, as set out in the news release dated June 23, 2026, remain unchanged.

Shareholder Loan

Further to the Company’s news releases dated March 26, 2026 and June 23, 2026, the Company also announces that 109 has further amended the terms of the loan owing to 599 in the principal amount of $1,401,632.29 (the “Loan”) to extend the maturity date of the Loan from November 30, 2026 to November 30, 2029. The terms of the Loan, as set out in the news releases dated March 26, 2026 and June 23, 2026, otherwise remain unchanged. No securities of the Company will be issued in connection with the Loan or the amendments described in this news release, and no bonus or other compensation is payable in connection with them.

Related Party Transaction

The amendments to the Loan and the Working Capital Adjustment Payment (collectively, the “Amendments”) constitute “related party transactions” pursuant to Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101") as Michael Irmen is Chief Executive Officer and a director of the Company and a director and controlling shareholder of 599, and Robert Scott is a director of the Company.

The Company is exempt from the formal valuation requirement in Section 5.4 of MI 61-101 in reliance on Section 5.5(b) of MI 61-101 as the Company is not listed on a specified market within the meaning of MI 61-101. Additionally, the Amendments are exempt from the minority approval requirement in Section 5.6 of MI 61-101 in reliance on Section 5.7(1)(f) of MI 61-101 as (i) the Loan and the Notes, as amended, are on reasonable commercial terms that are not less advantageous to the Company than if they were obtained from a person dealing at arm’s length with the Company, and (ii) neither the Loan nor the Notes, as amended, is convertible into, or repayable as to principal or interest in, equity or voting securities of the Company or a subsidiary entity of the Company, or otherwise participating in nature.

The Company did not file a material change report more than 21 days before the entering into of the Amendments as the terms of the Amendments were not settled until shortly prior to execution and the parties wished to close the Amendments on an expedited basis for sound business reasons.

About Ironman International Ltd.

Established in 1999, Ironman International Ltd. is a leading North American provider of horizontal directional drilling and trenchless infrastructure services, operating 24/7 to support residential, commercial, industrial, and utility clients. The Company specializes in delivering cost-effective, low-impact underground installation solutions across a broad range of applications, including telecommunications, electrical, water and sewer, oil and gas, geothermal, and irrigation systems. With a modern fleet of specialized equipment and an experienced technical team, Ironman is capable of executing complex projects across diverse and challenging environments, including lakes, rivers, coastal and near-shore marine installations, rail corridors, roadways, and highways. The Company also provides complementary services designed to enhance efficiency, maintain safety standards, and ensure projects are completed on time and on budget. The common shares of Ironman International Ltd. are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol “IMI” and trade on the OTCQB Venture Market under the symbol “IMITF”.

data.title: GTA VI Is Now a Spectator Sport. Of Course You Can Bet on It
data.description:
I thought the most Vice City thing you could do this week was drive a stolen car into the ocean and blame the handling. It turns out you can sit at home and take a financial position on when a man called TheBurntPeanut will finish Grand Theft Auto VI. The ocean can wait.

Polymarket displayed about US$131,000 in trading volume on its TheBurntPeanut finish-date market. That’s the value of trades, and the same shares can change hands more than once. Still, it’s a substantial amount of buying and selling over the question of when one Twitch streamer will be done with a video game.

Polymarket’s GTA VI page also lists contracts on when another streamer, ohnePixel, would finish and when Rockstar might release a PC version. The PC one I get. Millions of people would like a date from a company perfectly happy to let them keep asking. The Peanut one is more interesting because nearly everything that makes him worth watching can also make him take longer.

Please proceed directly to the plot

Rockstar spent years building a world in which wandering off is half the pleasure. Some of the best moments in these games start when you miss a turn, hear something good on the radio or decide, on evidence available only to you, that a particular car needs to be in a particular swimming pool. A deadline contract gives somebody watching at home a reason to look at that same swimming pool and think about the time.

Polymarket lists TheBurntPeanut’s Twitch channel as a resolution source. Its contract titles use the word “by,” which matters. Several dates can resolve Yes if he finishes early enough. The deadlines are separate propositions. For the viewer, the difference between finishing a game and continuing to play it is pleasantly blurry. For anybody settling a contract, it has to be sharp enough to pay out on.

Imagine buying Yes on a near deadline and then watching him discover a boat. Before you placed the bet, the boat was good television. You might even have been the person in chat demanding he steal it. Now you have the unfortunate experience of sincerely wanting a man in a video game to ignore a boat. You could have had that feeling for free by becoming somebody’s project manager.

The audience has a position

Sports betting already taught people to watch the last few minutes of a decided game because somebody still needs to score. A streamer’s schedule gives a market looser material. A broadcast can run late, stop early or turn into forty minutes of something the person playing finds hilarious. He’s also close enough to his viewers to read what they type. You can see the potential for a very strange chat window when some of the people in it would prefer he keep moving.

That’s a possibility, and the trading volume tells us about trades. It can’t tell us how a streamer played or why a particular viewer kept watching. The reason this market is worth a look is how cheaply it can change the stakes for the audience. A running joke, a detour, or a decision to call it a night can suddenly have a financial meaning for someone who has absolutely no say in any of it.

I wrote last week about how much ownership you get when you buy GTA VI. There is now a pleasantly absurd alternative. You can buy an interest in how quickly somebody else gets through his copy. I hope he takes the boat.

data.title: Argentina's 2026/27 wheat forecast may rise on strong yields
data.description:
Argentina's 2026/27 wheat production forecast, currently of 23.4 million metric tons, could be raised due to higher-than-expected yields as the harvest progresses, the Buenos Aires grains exchange said on Thursday.

  • The current harvest forecast is the country's second-highest on record

  • Argentina is a key global wheat exporter, and the crop has benefited this season from favorable rainfall and low temperatures

  • The exchange estimates average wheat yield at between 1.7 and 2.4 tons per hectare

  • It estimates 24.9% of the sown area has been harvested, and expects it to keep rising

  • "If these yields are sustained, an upward revision of the production forecast cannot be ruled out," the exchange said

  • Soybean planting for the 2026/27 cycle is 39.7% complete, while corn planting has reached 52.7%, according to the exchange

  • The exchange estimates the 2026/27 total soybean production at 53.6 million tons and projects the corn harvest to be of 66 million tons

data.title: Fortum Restructures Business, Leadership Team To Accelerate Customer-Led Growth
data.description:
HELSINKI (dpa-AFX) - Fortum Corporation (FORTUM.HE) announced a renewed business structure and leadership team on Thursday as part of efforts to accelerate customer-led growth, simplify governance and improve execution of its strategy.

The new operating model will take effect on February 1, 2027, with President and CEO Markus Rauramo continuing to lead the company. The structure will comprise three business units: Corporate Customers and Markets, led by Kati Levoranta; Consumer Solutions, headed by Mikael Rönnblad; and Generation, led by Mikael Lemström.

The enabling functions will include Finance, led by CFO Tiina Tuomela, Strategy and Innovation, for which a recruitment process will begin, and People, led by Karin Svenske Nyberg.

Current leadership team member Simon-Erik Ollus has decided to pursue opportunities outside Fortum following an agreed transition period.

Fortum said the changes will align its organization and resources more closely with customer needs while maintaining financial discipline, risk management and operational control. The revised structure will not affect its external financial reporting, and its existing reporting segments will remain unchanged for now.

The company sees near-term growth opportunities particularly in data centres, consumer markets and small and medium-sized businesses, while demand from metals, mining and other energy-intensive industries is expected to develop over the medium to long term.

Fortum will provide further details on its long-term strategy, growth ambitions and key performance indicators alongside its full-year results on February 2, 2027.

data.title: SK hynix Stocks Rise 2.23% as Seoul Chip Rebound Fades From a 5.7% Gain
data.description:
SK hynix shares rose 2.23% to 1,053,000 won at the November 26 regular-session close in Seoul, after climbing as much as 5.73% to 1,089,000 won in morning trade. The move recovered only a fraction of Wednesday's 11.1% plunge, which followed a 7.9% slide in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.

Two forces drove the rebound. The U.S. Trade Representative's Section 301 proposal kept South Korea at a 15% rate and exempted semiconductors, which already face product-specific duties, Seoul Economic Daily reported from Washington. Daishin Securities' Lee Kyoung-min called the plan a reaffirmation of the 15% level rather than a new negative. On demand, TrendForce still expects DRAM supply to stay tight through 2027 and DRAM revenue to rise 69% to $1.15 trillion, even after some Chinese cloud providers trimmed 2027 server DRAM orders.

The fade from a 5.7% morning gain to 2.2% at the close shows buyers are selective. SK hynix leans heavily on DRAM and HBM, so narrowing contract price gains in late 2027 would hit it directly. The GuruFocus chart shows a perfect GF Score of 100/100, with elite profitability, a strong balance sheet and powerful momentum. GF Value of 1,544,408 won implies a 31.8% discount, yet GuruFocus flags a possible value trap, consistent with peak-cycle earnings inflating the model. The next test is first-quarter 2027 contract price talks, the first read on whether DRAM price gains are narrowing as forecast.

data.title: Shelly Group’s Board of Directors reaffirms its support for Schneider Electric SE’s amended Offer
data.description:
Shelly Group SE/ Key word(s): Tender Offer

Shelly Group’s Board of Directors reaffirms its support for Schneider Electric SE’s amended Offer

26.11.2026 / 20:15 CET/CEST

The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

Shelly Group’s Board of Directors reaffirms its support for Schneider Electric SE’s amended Offer Sofia / Munich, November 26, 2026 – Shelly Group SE (Ticker: SLYG / ISIN: BG1100003166), a provider of IoT and smart building solutions based in Sofia, Bulgaria, announces that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has reaffirmed its reasoned opinion of October 5, 2026, on the voluntary tender offer (the “Offer”) by SE 2026 A SAS (the “Bidder”), an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Schneider Electric SE, as amended in line with the instructions of the Bulgarian Financial Supervision Commission (the “FSC”) in its resolution of October 22, 2026.

According to the Board of Directors, the Offer, as amended in line with the requirements of the FSC, fully reflects the terms agreed under the investment agreement announced on September 24, 2026, under which Shelly Group agreed to support a potential Offer. These include the offered price and the Bidder’s stated intentions, in particular its strategic plan for Shelly Group following a successful completion of the Offer, in respect of the management, geographical footprint, employment levels and the preservation of its core trademarks for a specific period of time, as well as in respect of the delisting of Shelly Group.

The amendments to the Offer do not change the offer price of EUR 70.00 per share as of the date the Offer was first registered with the FSC. Therefore, the Board has determined that the voluntarily commissioned independent fairness opinion (the “Fairness Opinion”), prepared by Freitag & Co. GmbH (“Freitag”) in connection with the originally registered Offer, remains current and may be relied upon in assessing the fairness of the offer price under the amended Offer. In addition, the date as of which the offer price is determined is the date of the initial registration of the Offer with the FSC (September 28, 2026), and the value of the shares in the Fairness Opinion was determined around that date. Freitag concludes that the offer price of EUR 70.00 per share in cash is fair, from a financial point of view, to the shareholders of Shelly Group.

A summary of the Fairness Opinion will be available at https://corporate.shelly.com/uploads/pages/Shelly_Opinion_Letter-efc356.pdf

The Offer is currently still subject to approval by the FSC. Upon approval of the Offer by the FSC, Shelly Group will publish the Board’s opinion together with the offer document as approved by the FSC. The acceptance period for the Offer will only commence upon publication of the offer document, as approved by the FSC.

Further information at corporate.shelly.com.

Shelly Group SE develops, designs, and distributes IoT and smart building solutions for DIY and professional users, offering advanced technology, seamless interoperability, and a high degree of technological flexibility. data.title: Weston Energy III LLC Provides Early Warning Disclosure Regarding Battery Mineral Resources Corp.
data.description:
New York, New York--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Weston Energy III LLC ("Weston III") announces that, on November 13, 2026, it acquired 50,090,500 common shares of Battery Mineral Resources Corp. ("BMR") from treasury at a price of CDN $0.20 per share, for aggregate consideration of CDN $10,018,100, pursuant to the initial closing of a non-brokered private placement by BMR (the "Offering") (the "Weston III Subscription").

The Weston III Subscription forms part of the initial closing of the Offering, pursuant to which BMR issued an aggregate of 77,294,125 BMR common shares at a price of CDN $0.20 per share for aggregate gross proceeds to BMR of CDN $15,458,825.

Immediately prior to the Weston III Subscription, Weston III did not own any BMR common shares. Immediately following completion of the Weston III Subscription:

  • Weston III directly owns 50,090,500 BMR common shares, representing approximately 10.1% of the outstanding BMR common shares; and

  • Yorktown Partners (as defined below) beneficially owns, controls or directs, directly or indirectly, an aggregate of 318,674,480 BMR common shares, representing approximately 64.3% of the outstanding BMR common shares, of which: (i) 50,090,500 are registered in the name of Weston III; (ii) 206,430,388 are registered in the name of Weston I (as defined below); (iii) 56,101,387 are registered in the name of Weston II (as defined below); (iv) 4,200,000 are registered in the name of Yorktown XI (as defined below); and (v) 1,852,205 are registered in the name of Windmark (as defined below).

The percentage calculations set out in this News Release are presented on an undiluted basis and do not take into consideration any common shares of BMR issuable upon the exercise of outstanding options or other convertible or exchangeable securities. The pre-closing percentages are calculated based on the 417,928,349 BMR common shares outstanding immediately prior to the completion of the Weston III Subscription, and the post-closing percentages are calculated based on the 495,222,474 BMR common shares outstanding immediately following completion of the Weston III Subscription (in each case, as reported by BMR).

Weston III is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. All of the outstanding voting equity interests of Weston III are owned by Yorktown Partners XII, L.P. ("Yorktown XII"), a limited partnership managed by Yorktown Partners LLC ("Yorktown Partners"), and Weston III is considered to be controlled by Yorktown XII under applicable securities laws in Canada. Accordingly, Yorktown XII is deemed to beneficially own the BMR common shares owned by Weston III.

Yorktown Energy Partners XI, L.P. ("Yorktown XI" and, together with Yorktown XII, the "Yorktown Entities") is also a limited partnership managed by Yorktown Partners. Each of Weston Energy, LLC ("Weston I") and Weston Energy II, LLC ("Weston II" and, together with Weston I and Weston III, the "Weston Entities") is considered to be controlled by Yorktown XI under applicable securities laws in Canada. Accordingly, Yorktown XI is deemed to beneficially own the BMR common shares owned by Weston I and Weston II, and each of Weston I and Weston II is deemed to beneficially own the BMR common shares owned by the other. Windmark Capital LLC ("Windmark") is an affiliate of Yorktown Partners.

As a result of the Weston III Subscription, Weston III's percentage securityholding in the BMR common shares increased from 0% to approximately 10.1%, and the aggregate number of BMR common shares beneficially owned, controlled or directed, directly or indirectly, by Yorktown Partners increased by 50,090,500 shares (from 268,583,980 shares to 318,674,480 shares). The aggregate percentage securityholding of Yorktown Partners remained approximately 64.3%.

The purchase price paid by Weston III for the 50,090,500 BMR common shares acquired pursuant to the Weston III Subscription was CDN $0.20 per share (CDN $10,018,100 in the aggregate), paid in cash.

The Weston III Subscription was completed by way of an issuance of BMR common shares from treasury pursuant to a subscription agreement between Weston III and BMR, dated November 13, 2026, on terms substantially consistent with those applicable to the other subscribers under the Offering. The Weston III Subscription was not effected through the facilities of any stock exchange.

The BMR common shares acquired by Weston III pursuant to the Weston III Subscription are subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day following the closing date of the Offering, in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws.

The BMR common shares acquired by Weston III pursuant to the Weston III Subscription were acquired for investment purposes. Each of Weston III and its joint actors may, from time to time in the future, increase or decrease its direct or indirect ownership, control or direction over BMR common shares or other securities of BMR through market transactions, private agreements, or otherwise, including by effecting acquisitions or dispositions of securities of BMR for cash or other consideration.

This News Release updates the information contained in the early warning report filed on December 13, 2021 on behalf of Yorktown Energy Partners IV, L.P. ("Yorktown IV"), Yorktown Energy Partners VI, L.P. ("Yorktown VI"), Yorktown XI, Weston I and Weston II. Each of Yorktown IV and Yorktown VI has since completed its windup and been dissolved, and neither of them currently owns any BMR common shares or is a joint actor in respect of the Weston III Subscription.

The Yorktown Entities and Weston Entities intend to file a report under National Instrument 62- 103 - The Early Warning System and Related Takeover Bid and Insider Reporting Issues setting out additional information concerning the Weston III Subscription. For further information and to obtain a copy of such report, please contact Mr. Bryan H. Lawrence at Yorktown Partners LLC, 20th Floor 410 Park Ave., New York, NY 10022-4407 or by telephone at (212) 515-2100.

The common shares of BMR are listed and posted for trading on the TSX Venture Exchange. The head office of BMR is located at 1021 W Hastings Street, 16th Floor, Vancouver, British Columbia V6E 0C3.

Each of the Yorktown Entities is a limited partnership formed under the laws of Delaware. In this News Release, Yorktown Partners, the Yorktown Entities, the Weston Entities, Windmark and the other limited partnerships and limited liability companies noted below in this section "About the Yorktown Group" are collectively referred to as the "Yorktown Group". Yorktown Partners is a private investment manager that, together with its affiliates and affiliated funds, invests in the energy industry with an emphasis on North American oil and gas production and midstream businesses. data.title: Powerful Storm Hits East Coast, Scrambling Thanksgiving Plans — WSJ
data.description:
By Victoria Albert

A major storm is scrambling Thanksgiving Day plans along the East Coast, with heavy winds and rain causing power outages, flight cancellations and the postponement of Macy's annual holiday parade.

The National Weather Service warned of major coastal flooding from Georgia up to the Northeast and wind gusts exceeding 50 mph. Heavy rainfall is also expected in the area, with 1 to 4 inches projected for the mid-Atlantic and 1 to 2 inches in southern New England.

As of early Thursday afternoon, more than 400,000 people were without power along the East Coast, according to Poweroutage.us. The outages were concentrated in Maryland and Virginia, where energy-provider Dominion said broken utility poles and large trees on power lines meant it could be days before power was restored in some areas.

"Outages are especially difficult on a holiday, and we appreciate your patience as our crews work to get the lights back on," the utility said on social media.

Another 130,000 power outages were reported in Missouri. The state is grappling with several inches of snow in some areas and a winter-storm warning.

Roughly 1,400 flights within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed, and 400 have been canceled, according to flight-data specialist FlightAware. The hardest-hit airport so far is Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Va.

In New York City, where fears of severe weather forced officials to postpone the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, wind gusts exceeding 30 mph were recorded across all five boroughs. The city's emergency-management department warned residents to secure loose outdoor items and use caution around trees and scaffolding.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned that the city could see wind gusts as high as 65 mph. "If you're traveling, give yourself extra time," Mamdani said Wednesday night. "And remember: No destination is worth risking your safety."

Write to Victoria Albert at victoria.albert@wsj.com

data.title: Keppel Says Proposed M1 Divestment Supports Asset-Light Strategy
data.description:
SINGAPUR (dpa-AFX) - Keppel Ltd. (KPELF.PK, KPELY.PK, BN4.SI) on Thursday said its proposed divestment of M1 through a merger with StarHub Ltd. would support its strategy to become more asset-light and monetize non-core assets by 2030, while allowing it to retain exposure to potential growth in Singapore's telecommunications market.

Under the proposed all-share transaction, Keppel expects to deconsolidate approximately S$324 million in M1 net debt and receive a 23% stake, comprising 546.5 million shares, in the enlarged StarHub.

Keppel CEO Loh Chin Hua described the transaction as a two-stage divestment, with the company planning to monetize its StarHub stake over time through market sales, a strategic or fund investor, or a distribution to shareholders.

Loh said retaining M1 as a subsidiary would require continued funding for technology upgrades, cybersecurity, network and spectrum costs. Keppel would also continue consolidating M1's financial results, including losses recorded in the first half of 2026.

Keppel said the all-share structure would allow the combined company to preserve cash for integration and growth, while enabling Keppel to participate in potential benefits from market consolidation and improved competitive conditions.

Keppel's profit contribution from M1 was S$3 million in FY2025.

data.title: Argentina's Mundial printing company files for bankruptcy protection with $5mn debt
data.description:
Argentine packaging and printing company Mundial S.A. has entered preventive insolvency proceedings with liabilities of ARS 7.67bn ($4.8mn), after a sharp decline in sales forced it to cut nearly 40% of its workforce and seek court protection to keep its Buenos Aires factory operating. The family-owned business, based in the Barracas district, filed for protection in September, and a commercial court opened the proceedings on October 20, La Nación reported.

The company, which produces printed packaging for industries including cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and food, saw nominal revenue fall from ARS16.97bn  in 2023 to ARS 8.61bn in 2025, a decline of about 49% over two years.

Mundial attributed its financial difficulties to weaker demand, rising input costs, changes in the printing market and higher borrowing expenses. It said it had relied on bank loans to maintain operations, but that financing strategy eventually worsened its liquidity problems.

The company's financial position had deteriorated significantly by September 2026. Central Bank records showed it owed ARS 3.36bn to seven financial institutions, all of which had assigned it credit-risk ratings between categories three and five.

Banco Nación was its largest bank creditor, with exposure of ARS 1.35bn, and classified Mundial in category five, the highest-risk rating. BBVA was owed nearly ARS 798mn, followed by Galicia with ARS 408mn, Supervielle with ARS 390mn and Banco Provincia with ARS 371 mn. American Express and Santander were also listed among its creditors.

More than 75% of the company's bank liabilities were in the two highest-risk categories. Its debt to BBVA was 161 days overdue, while American Express reported 91 days of arrears.

In its court filing, Mundial identified June 12, 2026, as the date on which it entered a state of default, following a demand from BBVA to settle an obligation of 105.4 million pesos. The company acknowledged that it had faced financial difficulties before that date but said it had tried to meet its commitments through alternative financing.

The downturn also led to substantial job cuts. Mundial had 89 employees at the end of August, according to documentation submitted to the court, after reducing its workforce by about 40%. It also had more than ARS 311mn pesos in rescheduled social security liabilities.

The company's difficulties culminated in a dispute with electricity distributor Edesur. In September, the utility demanded payment of ARS 27.76mn and warned it could disconnect the factory from September 14 over unpaid bills. Mundial sought an injunction, arguing that losing electricity would halt machinery, interrupt production and jeopardise deliveries to customers.

On September 16, the judge overseeing the insolvency case ordered Edesur not to cut power over debts incurred before the filing. Mundial was still required to pay electricity bills falling due afterwards.

Founded by the Bermatov family more than 55 years ago, the company grew from a small printing workshop into an industrial packaging producer. It moved to its current Barracas site after the family acquired two warehouses in 1981, expanding its facilities from about 160 to 1,200 square metres.

The court has set December 28 as the deadline for creditors to submit claims. The insolvency administrator, Viscarret y Asociados, will oversee the verification process as Mundial seeks to restructure its obligations to banks, suppliers and other creditors while maintaining production and preserving its remaining jobs.

data.title: Gold drifts lower as Fed rate-hike fears loom
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump unveils new tariffs over excess industrial capacity
  • Spot palladium up 1%
  • US markets closed for Thanksgiving holiday

By Ashitha Shivaprasad

Gold prices drifted lower on Thursday, as lingering inflation concerns and the market's growing expectations that the US Federal Reserve will hike interest rates again pressured the precious metal.

Spot gold was down 0.4% at $3,566.99 per ounce by 1901 GMT. Prices briefly fell below the psychologically important $3,500 level on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025.

US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.9% to $3,565.90.

"Spot gold is testing support around the mid-$3,000 region. Gold is unlikely to see a sustained rebound until markets sense that the Fed is nearing the end of its rate-hike cycle," said Han Tan, chief market analyst at Bybit.

"Bullion bulls are set to be kept on the back foot... But fresh risk-off events across global financial markets may support the precious metal, adding to persistent purchases from central banks."

Robust domestic demand is fuelling inflation in the US, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023, data showed on Wednesday. It reinforced expectations that the Fed will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

The Fed's first rate hike in three years was delivered in September.

While gold is traditionally viewed as an inflation hedge, elevated rates can weigh on the non-yielding asset.

Given that risks exist, "it is likely too early to call a bottom in gold, and indeed in the precious metals complex," analysts at TD Securities said in a note.

"Long-term, however, the yellow metal along with the precious metals complex should see significant upside. Indeed, gold prices will likely start trending towards $5,000/oz in the latter part of next year, as investors muse about easing policy rates," they said.

HSBC on Thursday said continued equity market weakness puts gold at risk of breaking below $3,400 per ounce.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on goods from 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union.

Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.8% to $41.54 per ounce, platinum gained 0.8% to $1,290.62 and palladium climbed 1.4% to $873.84 per ounce.

US markets were closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

data.title: US, Qatar to help Venezuela clear regional development bank arrears, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Venezuela in arrears with regional development banks IDB, CAF
  • Bridge loans from US to clear IDB arrears, Qatar seen aiding with CAF
  • Total arrears to both development lenders are about $4.16 billion

By Rodrigo Campos, Libby George, Mayela Armas and Cassandra Garrison

Venezuela is working on separate bridge loans with the US Treasury and Qatar to clear arrears owed to two regional development banks, a move that could unlock fresh multilateral financing for the cash-strapped country, four sources familiar with the discussions said.

The unusual arrangements would allow Venezuela to settle arrears that currently prevent the lenders from extending fresh credit, reopening a potentially important source of funding as the government seeks to revive the economy and re-engage with international financial institutions after years of crippling US sanctions.

Under one arrangement, the US Treasury would provide a bridge loan to clear Venezuela’s arrears to the Inter-American Development Bank, the sources said. Two of the sources said the funds would come via the Treasury's Exchange Stabilization Fund.

Caracas said in a document it owed the IDB $2.735 billion in principal and interest as of end-2025.

The US Treasury did not reply to a request for comment and the IDB declined to comment.

Two sources likened the transaction to an overnight loan: Treasury funds would clear the arrears, allowing the IDB to approve new lending, whose proceeds could then be used to repay the United States. Venezuela would ultimately remain responsible for the debt.

The IDB cannot lend into arrears, but is already discussing possible loans that could be approved after the arrears are cleared, two of the sources said.

One source said an initial operation under consideration would be made through the IDB’s Special Development Lending window and would exceed its $500 million cap, requiring a waiver. A second waiver would be needed because Venezuela does not currently have an International Monetary Fund programme.

SDL loans carry some of the IDB’s costliest terms, the source said.

BRIDGE FROM QATAR

Separately, Qatar is considering a bridge loan to help Venezuela clear arrears owed to CAF, the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean, two sources said.

Venezuela reported owing CAF $1.423 billion at the end of 2025.

The government's efforts to restore access to multilateral financing come as Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said in early November that Venezuela was negotiating with multilateral institutions over about $17 billion in public- and private-sector financing. On Tuesday, however, she put potential funding at $10 billion, without explaining the change.

The Venezuelan communications ministry, which handles all media queries for the government, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

CAF declined to comment, and Qatar's government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Calixto Ortega, Rodriguez's top economic adviser, said on state television on Tuesday that the government was in “advanced discussions” to clear its arrears with multilateral lenders, without adding details.

Venezuela this week put its public-sector liabilities at $237.5 billion at the end of 2025, equivalent to 242% of GDP, including $116.5 billion in commercial debt and $67.3 billion in nonfinancial obligations concentrated in state oil company PDVSA.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Stocks Edge Lower After Touching a 52-Week Low of $772.74
data.description:
Goldman Sachs shares edged lower by 0.62% to $801.03 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, after falling as much as 4.1% to $772.74, a new 52-week low, in morning trading. The close capped an 8% decline over the week, even though the bank released no bad news of its own.

The pressure links back to AI financing. On November 20, Goldman and Apollo priced about $44 billion of notes to fund GPUs for SpaceX, and SpaceX shares fell 11% over the same week. Goldman's own prime brokerage data showed hedge funds selling global tech at a record pace, News Minimalist reported on November 25. Hot October inflation data added to the strain, pushing CME FedWatch odds of a December rate hike to about 97%. The underlying business is still strong: third-quarter equities revenue rose 72%, and annualized return on equity reached 20.7% in the first nine months, above the 14% to 16% target.

At the close, shares sit 30.6% below the July high of $1,153.99 and trade just over 2 times tangible book, against a five-year average of 1.7 times. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 84/100, with strong profitability and momentum but a financial strength reading near the bottom of the scale, likely reflecting the leverage typical of a large bank. data.title: Microsoft Stocks Slip 1.25% While Nadella Backs Cheaper In-House AI Models
data.description:
Microsoft shares slipped 1.25% to $489.93 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, while comments from Satya Nadella on Microsoft's AI model strategy drew attention. Speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit, Nadella said Microsoft's in-house MAI models trailing OpenAI and Anthropic by three to six months is a great position if they use 5% to 20% of the compute. Shares had opened down 3.53% before recovering most of the loss.

Copilot already chooses among OpenAI, Anthropic and MAI models for each task, and Nadella said most users simply select the automatic option. He later wrote on X that "Outcome per dollar is the frontier," and argued AI should become a commodity like cloud computing. Microsoft announced seven MAI models at its Ignite conference on November 17. Its OpenAI agreement gives it royalty-free access to a frontier model until 2032, Windows Latest noted in its report.

The strategy speaks directly to the market's fear of runaway AI capex. If Copilot can run largely on cheaper in-house models, gross margins on AI products could hold up even as token prices fall. The GuruFocus chart shows a perfect GF Score of 100/100, with elite profitability, a strong balance sheet and top-ranked momentum. GF Value of $606.01 implies a 19.2% discount and a "modestly undervalued" label, an unusual opening for a company of this quality after the AI selloff. The next test is fiscal second-quarter results in January, where Copilot margins and Azure growth will show whether the cost-first approach is working.
